actions.reason: Revision of findings to integrate foundational comparisons of objectivity frameworks (Quantum Darwinism/SBS) with scrambling theory.
actions.summary: Information scrambling describes the rapid delocalization of quantum information across many-body degrees of freedom, which challenges local retrieval. However, this process does not inherently preclude the formation of objective records. Objectivity emerges when system states are redundantly encoded into an environment through decoherence, satisfying Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS). These two processes—scrambling (which hides information) and decoherence-based broadcasting (which reveals it)—act on different sectors of the Hilbert space, allowing for the coexistence of delocalized scrambling and publicly accessible classical records.
